newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to appeal Belgian court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Renault to appeal Belgian court ruling.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA said on Friday it would appeal a Belgian court ruling that it had violated Belgium's labour laws with the announcement in February of the Vilvoorde plant closure.
"Renault will appeal this ruling," the company said in a statement.
It reiterated that it believed it had fully complied with Belgian law in announcing the closure but said it would take up the consultation procedures deemed necessary by the court.

It said "these procedural elements" did not alter the fact that Renault needed to close the plant for economic reasons. "The tribunal's decision does not change Renault's decision to stop ordering vehicles from Renault Industrie Belgique on July 31, 1997," it said.
In Belgium, protesting workers clashed with police during a march to protest the closure of the plant, which employs 3,100 people.
